In my job, the type of work I do is rather diverse: one day I might be focused on reviewing, another day I might be concerned with revising, and then on another day I might need to build something from scratch. I can't use AI in *all* my work, but in instances where my work is repetitive and near-programmatic, I've been able to use AI to make it almost entirely programmatic. The best thing about AI right now is that it allows people to develop their own automation solutions relatively rapidly. Of course, there is some trial and error. The workflow you create will rarely be perfect the first time. But each successive time becomes easier, and the work becomes much faster. I've built agents and libraries of scripts to support them. And it really is just a great experience.
